standard.title: Nominal and ordinal data
standard.description: Acquire, validate and represent data for nominal and ordinal categorical and discrete numerical variables, to address a question of interest or purpose using software including spreadsheets; discuss and report on data distributions in terms of highest frequency (mode) and shape, in the context of the data
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can analyse data distributions and identify patterns in many-to-one displays (AC9M4ST02). They have not yet distinguished nominal, ordinal and discrete numerical variables or calculated and interpreted mode.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students acquire, validate and represent data for nominal, ordinal and discrete numerical variables; discuss distributions in terms of mode and shape.

nodes.label: Types of categorical data
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can distinguish nominal, ordinal and discrete numerical variables and explain the difference.
nodes.minimum_width: Classify given variables as nominal, ordinal or discrete numerical with an explanation for each.
nodes.typical_width: Classify a range of real-world variables; explain why ordinal data has order but not equal intervals; connect data type to appropriate display choices.
wider: Survey how data type determines analysis choices in contexts like surveys and scientific research
Investigate what information is lost when ordinal data is treated as nominal

response_modes.reason: The nominal/ordinal distinction is subtle and context-dependent. Multiple varied variables — some clearly nominal, some clearly ordinal, some ambiguous — help students develop the discrimination.

nodes.hinge_reason: Data type classification is required by Node 3 — students who cannot distinguish nominal from ordinal cannot select appropriate displays or justify their choices, collapsing the Mode B task.
success_criteria: Student correctly classifies given variables by data type
Student explains the key difference between nominal and ordinal data

nodes.label: Acquiring and validating data
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collect data for a question of interest, identify and address data quality issues.
nodes.minimum_width: Collect data for a stated question using a systematic method; identify at least one data quality issue (missing responses, inconsistencies) and describe how to address it.
nodes.typical_width: Design a data collection method appropriate for the variable type; validate data for completeness and consistency; use a spreadsheet to organise and check data.
wider: Investigate how surveys are designed to minimise response error
Compare data collected by different methods for the same question and analyse differences

response_modes.reason: Data validation requires students to apply a deliberate checklist: completeness → consistency → plausibility. Without an explicit scaffold, students skip validation steps and proceed with flawed data.

nodes.hinge_reason: Data quality determines the validity of every downstream step — students who skip validation proceed with flawed data that produces misleading distributions and unreliable mode calculations (Mode B phase collapse).
success_criteria: Student collects data using a systematic method
Student identifies and describes at least one data quality issue in a dataset

nodes.label: Representing data with software
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create appropriate data displays using spreadsheet software for their variable type.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a frequency table and a bar chart for a categorical variable using spreadsheet software.
nodes.typical_width: Select and create appropriate displays for nominal, ordinal and discrete numerical data using software; justify display choice based on variable type.
wider: Compare how the same data appears in different display types and explain which is most informative
Use software to create grouped frequency tables for discrete numerical data
success_criteria: Student creates an appropriate display for a given variable type using software
Student labels the display correctly including titles and axis labels

nodes.label: Mode and distribution shape
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the mode of a dataset and describe the shape of its distribution in context.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the mode of a dataset from a frequency table or display; describe whether the distribution is roughly symmetric or skewed.
nodes.typical_width: Calculate and interpret mode for nominal, ordinal and discrete numerical datasets; describe distribution shape (symmetric, skewed, bimodal) using data context; explain what the mode tells us about the data.
wider: Investigate real datasets (e.g. survey data, class data) where the mode is misleading or limited
Compare mode to other measures of centre: when is mode the best summary?

response_modes.reason: Distribution shape and mode interpretation are deeply context-dependent. Students need varied real datasets — not constructed examples — to understand what summaries actually tell us.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Real dataset analysis and comparison of summary measures gives advancing students genuine statistical reasoning territory.
success_criteria: Student identifies the mode from a display or table
Student describes the distribution shape using appropriate language
